title: Build a typed fetch API client in TypeScript — 3 turns
description: Three turns build a typed fetch client: turn 1 GET with generic types, turn 2 POST with body, turn 3 error handling.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `get<T>(path: string): Promise<T>` in `src/apiClient.ts`. Call `fetch(this.baseUrl + path, { headers: { 'Accept': 'application/json' } })`. If the response is not ok (response.ok === false), throw `{ status: response.status, message: response.statusText }` as an ApiError. Otherwise return `response.json()` as T. Run `npm test -- --forceExit`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now implement `post<T, B>(path: string, body: B): Promise<T>` — use method: 'POST', headers including Content-Type: application/json, and body: JSON.stringify(body). Same error handling as GET. Run `npm test -- --forceExit` and fix any failures.
Final check: run `npm test -- --forceExit` one more time. All 4 tests must pass. Make sure error objects match the expected shape: `{ status: number, message: string }`.
success_criteria: GET fetches correct URL and returns typed JSON
GET throws ApiError on non-2xx response
POST sends JSON body with correct Content-Type header
POST throws ApiError on server error
